theme: 3 terms for saving and sharing data in SwiftUI: a stored setting, a per-scene value and a shared object

terms.definition: A property wrapper that reads and writes a value in UserDefaults and updates the view when it changes.
terms.example: Use AppStorage for the dark mode switch, so it survives a restart.

terms.definition: A property wrapper that saves a small value for each scene, so a screen can restore its state later.
terms.example: Keep the selected tab in SceneStorage.

terms.definition: A property wrapper that reads an observable object that a parent view shared with all its children.
terms.example: Read the cart with EnvironmentObject, so we skip the init chain.

video.title: AppStorage, SceneStorage & EnvironmentObject | Day 152
video.description:
Learn to explain how SwiftUI saves and shares data: AppStorage, SceneStorage & EnvironmentObject, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
AppStorage - A property wrapper that reads and writes a value in UserDefaults and updates the view when it changes.
SceneStorage - A property wrapper that saves a small value for each scene, so a screen can restore its state later.
EnvironmentObject - A property wrapper that reads an observable object that a parent view shared with all its children.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 152 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

landscape.title: SwiftUI AppStorage, SceneStorage & EnvironmentObject | Day 152
landscape.description:
Explain AppStorage, SceneStorage & EnvironmentObject in SwiftUI by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
앱스토리지, 씬스토리지, 인바이런먼트오브젝트 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

AppStorage - A property wrapper that reads and writes a value in UserDefaults and updates the view when it changes.
한국어: 앱스토리지: UserDefaults의 값을 읽고 쓰며, 값이 바뀌면 뷰도 갱신해 주는 프로퍼티 래퍼

SceneStorage - A property wrapper that saves a small value for each scene, so a screen can restore its state later.
한국어: 씬스토리지: 화면이 나중에 상태를 복원할 수 있도록 씬마다 작은 값을 저장해 주는 프로퍼티 래퍼

EnvironmentObject - A property wrapper that reads an observable object that a parent view shared with all its children.
한국어: 인바이런먼트오브젝트: 부모 뷰가 모든 자식 뷰에게 공유한 관찰 가능한 객체를 읽는 프로퍼티 래퍼

In this video, Mina and Jake keep a settings switch and a selected tab after a restart, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain AppStorage, SceneStorage and EnvironmentObject in English?

dialogue.title: Keep my settings

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, my settings switch forgets its value when I restart the app.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Use AppStorage. It reads and writes a value in UserDefaults, and the view updates too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I added AppStorage for `dark`, and it stays now!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, the selected tab goes back to zero when the system closes the scene.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is a job for SceneStorage. It saves a small value for each scene.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can I save the whole cart with SceneStorage?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No, only small values. Keep the cart in a shared object.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do all the screens get the `Cart`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Put it in the environment, and read it with EnvironmentObject in each child view.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What if I forget to share it from the parent?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The app crashes when a view reads the EnvironmentObject. Share it first.
Use AppStorage for the dark mode switch.
